I have a couple questions:

1: Is the "al'" in her name signifying Malkieri royal blood? I seem to recall reading that at some point in one of the more recent books.

2: Are we sure she's alive? I didn't think the Aes Sedai made statues of living sisters.
--[[User:Al&#39;Lan Mandragoran|Al&#39;Lan Mandragoran]] 06:26, March 5, 2010 (UTC) al'Lan Mandragoran



No. The Melkieri "al" is on the given name, not the surname, and I think I recall the feminine version was "el". So you have "al'Lan Mandragoran", which indicates Malkieri monarchy, and "Rand al'Thor", which does nothing of the sort. I also seem to recall only the king and queen are given the "al" and "el" prefix, where as Isam, who's also Malkeri royal blood, would not have the "al". [[User:Astro Droid|Astro Droid]] 10:27, March 5, 2010 (UTC)

I have argued that she hailed from the Two Rivers due to her name. First of all, an al'-prefix on the surname is a Two Rivers tradition. Secondly, she likely lived after the destruction of Manetheren, since the Manetherenite referred to themselves with double "al" signalising heritage from father and grandfather, and for ladies "ay" signalising heritage from mother and grandmother; cf. Aemon al Thorin al Caar and Eldrene ay Ellan ay Carlan. In other words, Eleyan lived at the oldest shortly after the formation of Farashelle, the newly arisen kingdom that included the Two Rivers region, and at the youngest seven generations before present time, as no or few Andoran officials had been seen in that time, and how would the girl Eleyan then have been inspired to go to the White Tower and become Aes Sedai? She is most likely much, much older than that, though, as she's described as "ancient", plus, even if she left seven generations ago, she would likely still be alive.

All I'm sure of is her hailing from the Two Rivers region, and after the Trolloc Wars.
